column1: # The showcase manifest: what each file under docs/showcase/ is, how it is
# checked, and what it is checked against. One source of truth for four
# consumers that each used to carry their own copy of this list —
# which is how a human checks one by hand.
# Columns are tab-separated: name, search, tier, note.
#   name    the module name, which is the file stem: <name>.hthr in this dir.
#   search  `-L` dirs, comma-separated, or `-` for none. The importing file's
#           own directory is searched *first* and is never listed (see
#           `resolve` in crates/cli/src/loader.rs), so a showcase importing a
#           sibling showcase needs no entry for this directory — and must not
#           have one: `-L docs/showcase` puts this directory's `parser_core`
#           module in two search directories is an error rather than a
#             suite      the in-process prefix of crates/elab/tests/showcase_calculator.rs
#             test       included by some other in-process test target
#             test-only  in-process only: the CLI *cannot* check this file, and
#                        the note says which of the two reasons applies — a
#                        stem that is not an identifier (a hyphen), so it can
#                        never be a module, or a deliberate hole that only the
#             unchecked  nothing checks it, by design — the note says why
#   note    one line, for a reader deciding whether this file is evidence.
# A file under docs/showcase/ with no row here fails
# new showcase declares its tier once, here, instead of being findable only by

column4: The realized calculator: the same program as idealized.hthr, at the limit of what checks.

The finite-set half of the same argument; does not check.

Generator input: crates/cli/examples/relational_context.rs, driven by scripts/relational-context-demo. Its `rewrite_receive` is `{ ?rewrite }`, a hole the generator fills, so it does not check standalone.
